claims.text: Let \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) with \(q=n-r\), graded by degree, and write \(\bar h_k\) for the image of \(h_k\). Since \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\) and \(\bar h_k=\bar s_{(k)}=0\) for \(k>q\), every element of \(A\) is a polynomial in \(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q\). Its positive-degree part has no constant monomial, hence lies in \((\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q)\). Conversely each \(\bar h_k\) has positive degree, so \((\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_q)\subseteq A_+\). Therefore \[ A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q). \] (For \(q=0\), both sides are \(0\).)

For every ideal \(J_v\subseteq A\), \[ A_+J_v=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)J_v=\sum_{k=1}^{q}h_kJ_v. \] If \(J_v\) is \(\mathbb Z\)-spanned by its Schur classes \(s_\mu\), this subgroup is \(\mathbb Z\)-spanned by the Pieri products \[ h_k s_\mu,\qquad 1\le k\le q. \] By Pieri, \[ h_k s_\mu=\sum_{\substack{
u\supseteq\mu\

u, \] with terms outside the \(q^r\)-box equal to \(0\) in \(A\).
